title: What is known about 1RB1LA_1LC0RA_0LF0LD_1RE1LD_1RE0RB_---0LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LA_1LC0RA_0LF0LD_1RE1LD_1RE0RB_---0LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is almost all 1s: a few long solid blocks separated by single 0s. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps; an exact macro simulator (blocks of 16 cells) finds no halt in the first 1012 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 4,093 cells have been visited and 4,081 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.285). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.347).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>12</sup> steps
claims.text: An exact macro simulator (blocks of 16 cells) runs 1012 steps without a halt. The macro simulator cuts the tape into blocks of K cells, run-length codes them, and crosses a whole run at once when the head leaves it on the far side in the state it entered with; it agrees with the plain simulator tools/c/tmrun cell for cell.

claims.title: A chain of blocks, the last one halved
claims.text: At the moments the head reaches a new cell on the right in state B, the tape is solid blocks separated by single 0s; successive moments show the last block halved (114, 57, 28, 14 between steps 4.28·10<sup>7</sup> and 4.35·10<sup>7</sup>) while the blocks before it are rearranged.

claims.title: The halting state, seen from the run
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps state F was entered 93,754 times, always reading a 1 (F0 halts).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is a chain of long solid blocks separated by single 0s; the last block is halved over and over, each half moving into the block before it, and the chain is rebuilt, sometimes as a ladder of doubling lengths.

facts.text: No halt in an exact macro simulator (blocks of 16 cells).
The last solid block is halved again and again while the blocks before it are rearranged.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
No halt in the C simulator; 4,093 cells visited.

sections.heading: What the machine does
html: Stop the machine whenever its head first reaches a new cell on the right, in state B. With e for 10, around step 4.3·107:

Between the separating 0s the tape is solid. The last block is halved again and again (114, 57, 28, 14, …), and the blocks before it are rearranged at the same time (642 becomes 349 and 381 and 197 while 320 grows to 673 and 874): the machine is doing arithmetic on the list of block lengths. After some rounds the chain is rebuilt; one rebuilt chain, at step 55,813,373, is a ladder of nearly doubling lengths: 1^5 e 1^2 e 1^6 e 1^13 e 1^27 e 1^55 e 1^111 e 1^223 e 1^447 e 1^546 e 1^66 e e A>0.

Each halving passes over the block many times, so a round costs much more than the width of the tape; the visited width grows like a power of the step count near 1/3 (fitted 0.29 and 0.35 for the two sides at 109 steps). The density of 1s is close to 1: 4,081 of the 4,093 visited cells hold a 1 after 109 steps.

sections.heading: Where a halt would have to come from
html: The halting transition is F reading a 0. F is entered only from C reading a 0 (0LF), so a halt needs C to step left from a 0 onto another 0: two adjacent 0s. In the first 108 steps F was entered 93,754 times, every time on a 1. On a tape whose 0s are single, that is automatic; a halt needs a block of length 0 between two separators, or C reading the 0 just inside the left end of the tape.
Whether the halving arithmetic ever produces two adjacent 0s there is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.285). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.347).
After 109 steps the tape spans 4,093 cells (190 left of the start, 3,121 right), with a density of 1s of 0.997.
